title: Leveraging Multidisciplinary Team Strengths
audience: Basic science learners planning a multidisciplinary AI research team
objectives: Identify essential roles for a single-cell RNA-seq AI project.
Plan communication, glossary-building, and shared decision-making.
Design training, shadowing, collaboration-tool, and reproducibility processes.
Reflect on how multidisciplinary teams improve scientific AI work.

sections.name: Multidisciplinary Landscape
sections.purpose: Define team roles and possible tensions.
sections.how_to_use: Fill out five role forms, then describe competing priorities and an organizational structure.

sections.name: Communication Strategies
sections.purpose: Plan communication norms and shared language.
sections.how_to_use: Write a meeting/documentation plan, define glossary terms, and list strategies to keep biology central.

sections.name: Team-Based Decision-Making
sections.purpose: Practice evaluating competing scientific AI approaches.
sections.how_to_use: Compare unsupervised discovery with supervised marker-based classification, then document a decision process.

sections.name: Training Opportunities
sections.purpose: Plan cross-training between computational and biological experts.
sections.how_to_use: Draft training, shadowing, and external learning plans.

sections.name: Collaboration Tools
sections.purpose: Choose tools and protocols for distributed project work.
sections.how_to_use: Select tools, describe sharing protocols, and draft a weekly dashboard.

sections.name: Reflection
sections.purpose: Connect team structure to adoption, effectiveness, and reproducibility.
sections.how_to_use: Reflect on integration barriers, team-success metrics, and reproducibility processes.

chatbot_guidance: When asked how to use this notebook, guide the learner through role design, communication, decision-making, training, tools, and reflection.
For basic science users, connect team roles to single-cell biology, data quality, interpretation, and reproducibility.
Help learners make team plans concrete rather than generic.
